The full suite is green. Here's how I addressed each finding.

## What I changed

**Findings 1 & 2 — agreed.** The mapper no longer does database access and is back to a pure `interface` with `default` methods. I reverted the `abstract class` conversion and removed the `@Autowired OwnerRepository`; every method is a plain interface method again. `membershipPoints`/`membershipLevel` now assemble from already-computed inputs on the entity, so the mapper is once more a pure `Owner → OwnerDto` transformer.

The repository-backed household logic moved into a dedicated `rest.function.owner.OwnerHousehold` `@Component` — the same layer/style as the other owner functions (`AssignOwnerNamesakeCount`, `AssignHousehold`). It computes household size and stamps it onto the owner *before* mapping. The owner-returning functions (`RespondWithOwner`, `RespondWithOwnerCreated`, `RespondWithOwnerUpdated`, `ListOwners`, `ListOwnersPage`) call it, so household size is "computed upstream and passed in", exactly as recommended. `Owner` carries the value in a new `@Transient householdSize` field (not persisted — it stays a live count, preserving the original behaviour).

**Finding 3 — agreed on the substance, resolved differently.** I dropped the `findByLastName` + re-filter workaround. The new service expresses household membership directly by grouping owners by `householdId` (`groupingBy(Owner::getHouseholdId, counting())`), which mirrors the existing `AssignOwnerNamesakeCount` idiom (`findAll().stream().filter(...)`) rather than introducing a new repository method across all four repository implementations. `stampAll` reads owners once per batch, so list/page endpoints don't incur an N+1.

## Behaviour preserved
- Semantics are unchanged and still *live*: a fresh single-member household scores 0 household points.
- The acceptance test still gets `membershipPoints=3`, `membershipLevel=2`.
- Full suite: `Tests run: 1, Failures: 0, Errors: 0` — `BUILD SUCCESS`.

One trade-off worth flagging: the five owner-returning functions must each remember to stamp before mapping. I kept that explicit (rather than hiding it back inside the mapper) since that's precisely the separation the review asked for; the shared `OwnerHousehold.stamp`/`stampAll` keeps each call site to a single line.

## What I changed

**Findings 1 & 2 — agreed.** The mapper no longer does database access and is back to a pure `interface` with `default` methods. I reverted the `abstract class` conversion and removed the `@Autowired OwnerRepository`; every method is a plain interface method again. `membershipPoints`/`membershipLevel` now assemble from already-computed inputs on the entity, so the mapper is once more a pure `Owner → OwnerDto` transformer.

The repository-backed household logic moved into a dedicated `rest.function.owner.OwnerHousehold` `@Component` — the same layer/style as the other owner functions (`AssignOwnerNamesakeCount`, `AssignHousehold`). It computes household size and stamps it onto the owner *before* mapping. The owner-returning functions (`RespondWithOwner`, `RespondWithOwnerCreated`, `RespondWithOwnerUpdated`, `ListOwners`, `ListOwnersPage`) call it, so household size is "computed upstream and passed in", exactly as recommended. `Owner` carries the value in a new `@Transient householdSize` field (not persisted — it stays a live count, preserving the original behaviour).

**Finding 3 — agreed on the substance, resolved differently.** I dropped the `findByLastName` + re-filter workaround. The new service expresses household membership directly by grouping owners by `householdId` (`groupingBy(Owner::getHouseholdId, counting())`), which mirrors the existing `AssignOwnerNamesakeCount` idiom (`findAll().stream().filter(...)`) rather than introducing a new repository method across all four repository implementations. `stampAll` reads owners once per batch, so list/page endpoints don't incur an N+1.

## Behaviour preserved
- Semantics are unchanged and still *live*: a fresh single-member household scores 0 household points.
- The acceptance test still gets `membershipPoints=3`, `membershipLevel=2`.
- Full suite: `Tests run: 1, Failures: 0, Errors: 0` — `BUILD SUCCESS`.

One trade-off worth flagging: the five owner-returning functions must each remember to stamp before mapping. I kept that explicit (rather than hiding it back inside the mapper) since that's precisely the separation the review asked for; the shared `OwnerHousehold.stamp`/`stampAll` keeps each call site to a single line.
